lines.t: Yeah…
This for the boy inside the man,
The one nobody saw.
Listen.
Little house, little heart on freeze,
Daddy loud, mama praying on her knees.
Learned quick: be quiet, just appease,
So I buried every question, put my pain on a leash.Mirror on the wall never answered what I’m worth,
Just echoed every wound I’d collected from my birth.
Every shout, every silence, every curse, every word,
Wrote a script in my chest, turned my soul into a blur.“Be tough, don’t cry, don’t talk, don’t feel,”
“Be strong, don’t fail, keep everything sealed.”
So I built a little throne out of anger and steel,
Told myself, “I’m a man, I don’t need to heal.”Church on Sunday, but I lived in the dark,
Heard about the cross, didn’t let it hit my heart.
Played good boy, but I kept all the parts
That were eating me alive, tearing me apart.
I’ve been running from the mirror, hiding all the pain,
Drinking for the courage, drowning in the shame.
Using women as my bandage, praise as cocaine,
But the idol in the mirror’s been the one that really reigned.YahuShua, can You hear me? I’m exposed in every scar,
Been worshiping myself and I’ve called it “who we are.”
Take this mask, this throne, this prison that I built,
Break me at Your feet and wash away this guilt.
High school halls, heartbeat like a kick,
Every girl a verdict, every stare another brick.
Talking to a queen felt like jumping off a cliff,
So I poured up shots just to maybe get a kiss.Red cups, loud room, sin in the air,
Took shots ’til the social anxiety was bare.
If the homies said, “She bad,” I felt like a heir,
If they laughed at my loss, I disappeared in despair.Porn on the screen when the nights got long,
Teaching me love is just bodies in a thong.
Scrolling feeds, flex culture so strong,
Told myself, “You’re a man if they say you belong.”Girls as trophies, not daughters of a King,
Chased curves, not character, not a covenant ring.
Used their beauty like a mirror to upgrade my bling,
But woke up next day feeling emptier within.
I’ve been looping all these memories like a cursed playlist,
Every childhood script keeps my soul in a fist.
Using women for my worth, brothers for applause,
But the idol in the mirror is the root of all my flaws.YahuShua, can You hear me? I’ve been fronting as a king,
But I’m just a broken boy trying to hide a fragile thing.
Tear these crowns down, burn the altars that I raised,
I am done with self-worship—let Your holy fire blaze.
Thought they were the problem—
All the women, all the friends, all the fake, all the noise.
But the face in the glass was the snake with the poise,
Striking my own soul while I smiled with the boys.Blamed my dad, blamed the world, blamed every ex,
Blamed God for the chaos and the wreck.
But Your voice cut through, put a sword to my chest,
“Son, the god that you serve is the self you protect.”Every “W” with women, every nod from the crew,
Only fed my addiction, kept me far from You.
I chased “that dude” more than being a dad,
Let my kids see a mask, not the wounds that I had.You said, “Look in the mirror, don’t move, don’t blink,
If I’m not on the throne, you’ll die in this drink.
She is not your savior, and the crowd’s just a wave,
If you don’t bow now, all you build is a grave.”
I’ve been running from the mirror, but You caught me in the dark,
You exposed my secret altars, lit a torch to every mark.
Women were my idols, men’s applause my favorite drug,
But You shattered all my statues with a crucified love.YahuShua, take this heart, make it husband, make it dad,
Make it servant in a world that’s completely going mad.
I renounce every idol, every loop, every lie,
I belong to You forever—let my old self die.
